nodes.summary: Let $0 < p \le 1/2$. For each $n$, let $B_n$ be a random $n \times n$ real matrix on a probability space $(\Omega_n, P_n)$ whose $n^2$ entries are mutually independent and each equal to $1$ with probability $p$ and to $0$ with probability $1 - p$. Then there is a function $o : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $o(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that $P_n(\det B_n = 0) = (1 - p + o(n))^n$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Singularity probability of Bernoulli matrices

nodes.summary: For each $n$, let $M_n$ be a random $n \times n$ real matrix on a probability space $(\Omega_n, P_n)$ whose $n^2$ entries are mutually independent and each have the Rademacher law, with mass $1/2$ at each of $1$ and $-1$. Then there is a function $o : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $o(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that $P_n(\det M_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(n))^n$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Singularity probability of Rademacher matrices

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $M$ be a matrix over $\mathbb{K}$ whose rows and columns are indexed by finite sets $n$ and $m$. Its smallest singular value is the real number $\sigma_{\min}(M) = \inf_{x \in \mathbb{K}^m,\ \lVert x \rVert_2 = 1} \lVert Mx \rVert_2$, where $\lVert \cdot \rVert_2$ is the Euclidean norm. When $m$ is empty there are no unit vectors, and $\sigma_{\min}(M) = 0$.
nodes.title: Smallest singular value of a matrix

nodes.summary: The Rademacher measure is the probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ that assigns mass $1/2$ to $1$ and mass $1/2$ to $-1$.
nodes.title: Rademacher measure on the real line
